blocks.task_summary: Prove that the sum of three consecutive integers n-1, n, n+1 is always divisible by 3.

evidence.basis: (n-1) + n + (n+1) (A1); 3n (A1); which is always divisible by 3 AG [2 marks]

blocks.task_summary: Prove that the sum of the squares of three consecutive integers n-1, n, n+1 is never divisible by 3.
method_path: Argue 3n² is divisible by 3 but 2 is not, so sum is never divisible by 3
accepted_alternatives: Observe 3n² is divisible by 3 and 2 is not, therefore 3n² + 2 is never divisible by 3
Divide by 3 to obtain n² + 2/3, not an integer

evidence.basis: (n-1)² + n² + (n+1)² = ... (A1); attempts to expand either (n-1)² or (n+1)² (M1); 3n² + 2 (A1); demonstrating recognition that 2 is not divisible by 3 … hence the sum of the squares is never divisible by 3 AG (R1) [4 marks]
